newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sumitomo Bank Thai unit sees 30 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Bank Thai unit sees 30 pct growth.

text.p: Sumitomo Bank Ltd's Thai branch is expecting a 30 percent increase in profits and lending growth in 1997/98 (April-March), its country general manager Kozo Yoneda told Reuters on Monday.
"We are now in discussions with our head office and making our budget for next year but I think loan growth and profits will grow at least 30 percent," he said.
The bank's financial year runs from April to March.
Yoneda declined to give a profit projection for this financial year nor did he give figures for last year.

The bank's Thai operation's total outstanding loans are worth $5.7 billion, he said. Outside of Japan, Thailand was the bank's most significant market in Asia behind Hong Kong and Singapore, he added.
Concerns surrounding the slowing Thai economy were overblown and the current difficulties were typical of a period of transition to more stable economic growth patterns, he said.

The bank counts a number of blue chip Thai corporates among its client base including members of the giant Charoen Pokphand conglomerate and firms engaged in automobiles, petrochemicals, steel and brewing.
